name: Cold waves & winter storms
summary: No top-tier cold or winter-storm warning across a major region found on 14 Nov; UK cold risk raised by weak polar vortex
state: Searches on 14 Nov found no top-tier cold or winter-storm warning across a major region and no cold-related power or gas outages. The low that crossed the US Northeast on 12–14 Nov brought mostly rain to the big coastal cities, with snow confined to higher ground. The trend stays up because the Met Office said on 7 Nov that the stratospheric polar vortex is weakening, which raises the chance of UK cold later in November without guaranteeing it (Irish News, PA).
for_you: No widespread cold disruption is under way. People in the UK can follow Met Office warnings and UKHSA cold-health alerts as late November approaches; older people and those in poorly heated homes are most exposed.
rubric_hit: No major cold wave or winter storm affecting large populations: Normal line

sources.title: The Irish News (PA) — UK faces increased risk of cold snap as polar vortex weakens

why: Severe cold and winter storms kill, cut power and spike gas demand, as in Texas in 2021; they matter most when energy supplies are tight.
drivers: Polar vortex disruption, blocking highs, ENSO, Arctic outbreaks.

rubric.alert: Deadly cold or winter storms with widespread power or gas outages.
rubric.watch: Top-tier cold or winter-storm warnings across a major region, or a cold wave lifting gas demand sharply.
rubric.normal: No major cold wave or winter storm affecting large populations.
